variants.headline: A bargain with {{partner}}
body: Our envoys have struck a trade deal with {{partner}}. We agreed to provide {{weGive}} and receive {{weGet}} in return. Merchants in {{terms.civilization}} say the terms match what was promised at the talks.

variants.headline: A bargain with {{partner}}
body: We are informed that a treaty of commerce was lately concluded between {{terms.civilization}} and {{partner}}.
Our side provides: {{weGive}}.
{{partner}} provides: {{weGet}}.

variants.headline: Hear it! Terms are struck with {{partner}}
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! Under the deal with {{partner}}, our side provides {{weGive}}, and theirs provides {{weGet}}.

variants.headline: A successful deal with {{partner}}
body: Read the terms for yourself, {{terms.civic.people}}. Our envoys agreed to provide {{weGive}} and secured {{weGet}} from {{partner}} in return. Give them their due for bringing home a favorable agreement.

variants.headline: A gift arrives from {{partner}}
body: We have received {{weGet}} from {{partner}}. The {{terms.civic.government}} asked for nothing but goodwill in return.

variants.headline: We give {{weGive}} to {{partner}} as a gift
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has sent {{weGive}} to {{partner}} with no terms attached. {{partner}} has issued an appreciation letter.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} strikes a trade route from {{originCity}} to {{destinationCity}}
body: Raiders under {{plunderer}} struck a shipment from {{originCity}} bound for {{destinationCity}}, and the goods are lost. Merchants in {{originCity}} are reviewing orders that depended on the load, and buyers in {{destinationCity}} will have to wait for another shipment, if one is sent.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} robs a route bound for {{destinationCity}}
body: Raiders under {{plunderer}} struck a shipment from {{originCiv}} before it reached {{destinationCity}} and carried off the load. The goods were meant for merchants in {{destinationCity}}, and the loss will be felt at the counter before the next delivery arrives.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} takes {{gold}} gold from a route to {{destinationCity}}
body: Raiders under {{plunderer}} struck a shipment from {{originCity}} bound for {{destinationCity}} and took {{gold}} gold. Merchants in {{destinationCity}} will count the loss in the next accounts, and buyers may find fewer goods on offer until the route is used again.

variants.headline: Trade needs a guarded route
body: Raiders under {{plunderer}} took a shipment from {{originCiv}} meant for our buyers. The {{terms.civic.government}} should say how it plans to protect the next one. Guarding a trade route costs money, and so does losing the goods.

variants.headline: The route from {{originCity}} is plundered
body: Word came that a shipment from {{originCity}} never arrived in {{destinationCiv}}. Raiders under {{plunderer}} struck it on the way, and the goods are gone. Our market will feel the gap, and merchants in {{originCity}} will wait on word of the next shipment.

variants.headline: Our outgoing trade has stopped
body: The last road our merchants used for trade beyond our borders has closed, and no caravan of ours sets out on it now. Bales packed for foreign buyers sit under sheeting in the warehouses. At the depot, the loading master has hung his tally board on a nail and given his crew leave to look for other work.

variants.headline: The weights are put away
body: The road to the foreign market served our merchants well while it lasted, and this season it stands idle. In its best years it carried our goods out and foreign coin back, and the yard that provisioned it worked by lamplight. The keeper of the scales has wrapped the weights in oilcloth and shut the chest.

variants.headline: Small exporters have less room to wait
body: At the last count {{routes}} roads of ours ran to foreign markets; this week the number is none. A merchant with goods already crated has nowhere to send them, and the workshop that cannot store a season of work will be first to let a hand go. Whoever let the final road close owes those shops an account of the cause and a date when another opens.

variants.headline: Notice to those who send trade out
body: Notice to shippers and warehouse keepers: no road of ours now runs to a foreign market. Store finished goods dry and counted, and take no new orders until a route is announced. The workshops continue; the warehouses hold.

variants.headline: Trade run complete from {{originCity}} to {{destinationCity}}
body: A trade run from {{originCity}} to {{destinationCity}} has finished. The cities are {{routeDistance}} tiles apart. Another run would give merchants at both ends time to line up new orders.

variants.headline: The next order from {{destinationCity}}
body: Our traders have finished the run from {{originCity}} to {{destinationCity}}. A repeat order from {{destinationCity}} would give workshops in {{originCity}} a reason to set aside stock for the next run.

variants.headline: A long route ends at {{destinationCity}}
body: Traders from {{originCity}} in {{originCiv}} have completed their run to {{destinationCity}}. Merchants in both cities will be watching to see if the route is used again.

variants.headline: A trade run between {{originCiv}} and {{destinationCiv}} enters the record
body: The trade record has a completed run from {{originCity}} in {{originCiv}} to {{destinationCity}} in {{destinationCiv}}. The two cities are {{routeDistance}} tiles apart.

variants.headline: Long trade route links {{originCity}} and {{destinationCity}}
body: A {{routeDistance}} trade route is now open between {{originCity}} ({{terms.civilization}}) and {{destinationCity}} ({{destinationCiv}}). In both cities, merchants and travelers are busily preparing for their next trip.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} strikes our trade route to {{destinationCity}}
body: Raiders under {{plunderer}} struck one of our shipments bound for {{destinationCity}}, and its load is lost. Merchants from {{originCity}} are reviewing orders that depended on the missing cargo. Buyers in {{destinationCity}} will have to wait for another shipment, if one is sent.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} takes our goods on the route to {{destinationCity}}
body: {{plunderer}} stripped one of our outbound shipments on the route to {{destinationCity}} and kept the goods. Our traders returned with empty hands and a full story. The merchants of {{originCiv}} and the buyers in {{destinationCity}} will feel this week's loss; the men who signed the papers will feel none of it.

variants.headline: The account of a plundered route
body: Shipments lost: one, and it began at {{originCity}}.
Raiders: {{plunderer}}.
Route: ours, bound for {{destinationCity}}.
Gold taken: {{gold}}.
Cargo: gone. The loss is entered beside the route that was struck.

variants.headline: Trade route to {{destinationCity}} plundered
body: Raiders under {{plunderer}} robbed a shipment of ours on the route to {{destinationCity}}. The merchants in {{originCity}} who sent it are notifying buyers in {{destinationCity}} that the load will not arrive. A late shipment is better than a rumor, and the buyers should hear the facts directly.

variants.headline: Send guards with the trade
body: {{plunderer}} took one of our shipments to {{destinationCiv}}, {{terms.civic.people}}. Put guards with the next shipment and make raiders think twice about the cost of taking it.

variants.headline: First foreign trade route opened
body: For the first time, our trade network has {{routes}} outgoing routes. Carts are carrying goods toward foreign markets. {{terms.civilization}}'s merchants are eager to learn from these early journeys, while the {{terms.civic.government}} is counting for their profits.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our trade roads are open
body: Hear it, people of {{terms.civilization}}! Our goods now travel to foreign markets by {{routes}} trade routes. Our merchants carry our goods beyond {{terms.civilizationAdjective}} borders, and money is pouring in!

variants.headline: What a new market can do for one kiln
body: The new roads abroad number {{routes}}, and the useful question is what they change for a single workshop at home. A potter who fires one order a month must still heat the kiln through, and a second buyer on the same firing pays for the heat twice over. The {{terms.civic.government}} has opened the way; the potters must make the ware worth the journey.

variants.headline: The road out stands open
body: A road with no cart is only a long walk. Ours comes home heavy.

variants.headline: Our forces seize goods from {{originCiv}}
body: Our soldiers stopped a foreign shipment from {{originCiv}} to {{triggerValues.we-plunder-foreign-trade-route.destinationCiv}} and seized its goods. The cargo is now in our hands, earing a considerable income for {{terms.civic.government}}. The government of {{destinationCiv}} has protested this incident.

variants.headline: {{gold}} gold taken from a foreign route
body: Our soldiers took {{gold}} gold from a shipment out of {{originCity}} along with its goods. The sum will help balance this month's books, and the merchants who lost it will remember the route and the men who held it.

variants.headline: A route from {{originCity}} to {{destinationCity}} is plundered
body: Reports from abroad relate that our soldiers stopped a shipment bound from {{originCity}} to {{destinationCity}} and brought it in with its goods. The cargo will sell well at our markets, and the officers may expect their share of praise. A great power takes what it intends to keep, and this cargo we intend to keep.

variants.headline: Foreign trade turns a profit
body: Merchants wait years for trade with {{originCiv}} to pay. A soldier with a good route can collect the same profit before supper.

variants.headline: Have we no merchants left?
body: Sir, we have spent years building trade on routes like the one from {{originCiv}} to {{destinationCiv}}, and our soldiers have just struck one of them. The loss is not only the goods but the trust that sent them. When we want that route again, the merchants at the far end will remember whose flag stopped their goods.
